OmaTasks now caps how much it reads from Todoist. A broken or compromised server can no longer fill the shell's memory with an endless response. Nothing changes in the panel, the bar, or Quick Add.

## Fixed

- **A Todoist response can no longer exhaust the shell's memory.** Requests used QML's `XMLHttpRequest`, which keeps the whole response in the shell before the plugin can look at it, so the 20-second timeout limited how long a request ran but not how much it kept. Each request now runs in a short `Fetch.py` process using the system Python, which stops reading at 16 MB and hands the shell at most that. A larger answer shows "Todoist sent more data than OmaTasks reads at once" and the sync retries later, keeping your tasks on screen. The helper receives the request and API token on its standard input, never its command line, and does not follow redirects. By @crmne; thanks @HANCORE-linux for the report in [omacom/omarchy-plugin-marketplace#12072](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-plugin-marketplace/issues/12072).

## Known limitations

- Each request starts a Python process, which adds a few tens of milliseconds to syncing and saving.
- An account whose full sync is larger than 16 MB cannot sync until it is smaller.

## Validation

111 JavaScript tests, 24 composer UI checks, and 18 list interaction checks passed. QML parsing, shell syntax checks, and Omarchy plugin validation also passed. `Fetch.py` was run against a local server sending an endless response, a declared length over the cap, a body exactly at the cap, a rate limit, and a redirect. The service was also run in Quickshell against a local server: it synced normally, and when the server offered 2 GB the shell stayed under 100 MB and reported the error.

## Install

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omatasks.git --enable
```

Requires Omarchy Quattro and a Todoist account. Existing users can update the plugin through Omarchy.
